title: Portfolio Update & 1 Year of Hated Moats
snippet: Welcome to our portfolio update for July 2026 and earnings call for our first full year on Substack!
content_html:
Dear Hated Moats shareholders (our Substack subscribers),

This week, it’s been 1 year since our launch on this platform. Here are results of the growth in our Q3, as well as performance of our portfolios. :)

1. Our Q4 & First Year in Numbers

For reference, our Q3 report was posted on May 4, 2026 here:

1.1. Production

The output split of publications in this quarter looks like this:

  • Deep Dives: 3

  • DCFriday: 4

  • Other Articles: 8

That’s 15 articles, the same amount as during Q3 2026. We managed to post one more deep dive than in previous quarter but it’s still not enough - these past couple of months have been research heavy and we are preparing more than 5 deep dive analyses at the same time though!

Excluding this very article, we published total of 80 articles in our first year. Not too bad!

1.2. Growth

1.2.1. Substack

The growth has slowed but that’s what one should expect as time goes by I believe. There were periods of almost no growth at all which frankly scared me for a bit there, and generally, it got much more cyclical, coming in waves:

Base: April 29: 3,100

Growth in Q4:

May 14: 3,200

May 28: 3,300

June 19: 3,400

June 29: 3,500

July 12: 3,600

July 25: 3,700

July 28: 3,751

That’s +651 net new subscribers, slowly approaching the 4,000 level. That’s 21% growth ( down from +34.8% previous quarter) and 7.23 subscribers per day (down from 8.5 per day in Q3). So yes, the growth has obviously slowed but we’re still happy for every single one of you joining!

1.2.2. Twitter

We wrote this in our previous earnings call:

“Twitter as a platform is officially dead for our type of content”.

… and the more time passes, the more true that statement becomes. We went from 11,655 followers on April 30, 2026 to 12,919 followers on July 31. We won’t even waste your precious time and our precious space with talking about this platform anymore. :)

Subscribe now

1.2.3. Overall Growth in 1st Year

We believe that getting to over 3,700 free subscribers on Substack and almost 13,000 followers on Twitter in one year is still an amazing result. Don’t really care about Twitter but what we managed to achieve here is quite remarkable and we’re really thankful for all of you joining!

1.3. Earnings

  • Substack: avg. 7.23 new subscribers per day (est. 7 new subscribers per day):

    ✔️ BEAT

  • Twitter: avg. 14 new followers per day (est. 10 new followers per day): ✔️ BEAT

(period of April 29, 2026 - Jul 28, 2026)

Twitter was a beat despite being dead due to our modest expectations and we hit Substack estimate almost exactly. We’ll work hard to increase avg subscriber gain towards the long-term goal of 10 new free subscribers per day.

1.3.1. Strategic Focus from Q3

How we’ve done with our plans from previous quarters?

  • Hated Moats Website Launch - ✔️ , you can check it out at www.hatedmoats.com

  • Valuation Map & Editor

    • Valuation Map: ✔️ = it’s LIVE and it looks sick!

    • Valuation Editor: ❌ = still in the process of being developed

  • Hated Moats IPO - ❌ = has not happened yet as we want these to be ready, finished and useful: Valuation Editor and Hated Moats Watchlist up and running. We expect IPO sometime during the next quarter though!

  • Stay consistent -✔️ = we indeed published (more than) 1 article per week!

Beating estimates for the quarter, launching the website and developing Valuation Map and remaining consistent with the core - publishing, we are overall happy with this quarter. Valuation Editor is in its development, Watchlist is being design as we speak and Hated Moats IPO is on its way!

1.4. Guidance for Q1 2027

(period of July 29, 2026 - Oct 28, 2026)

1.4.1. Growth

For Q1 FY2027, we expect following growth while we raise guidance to:

  • Substack: avg. 8 new subscribers per day

  • X (Twitter): avg. 12 new followers per day

1.4.2. Strategic Focus for the next quarter

  • Stay consistent - the most important one which we managed to fulfill and we’ll try our best to keep going!

  • Launch Valuation Editor - the truly interactive part of Hated Moats, and we really want this one running ASAP

  • Launch Hated Moats Watchlist - useful series with regular updates, we are working hard on building the methodology right now

  • Hated Moats IPO - eventually, run the initial paid offering, i.e. provide even more value to those who are intested in the paid tier of this publication

Share

All in all, this was a good quarter, and a good year for Hated Moats, and we are very grateful for you, a curious mind reading this article! Let’s go for a strong second year together! And now, let’s have a peak how we actually performed in the markets!

2. Portfolio Update

Remember that this quarter, we launched:

www.hatedmoats.com

- on the website, you can always check-out the portfolios in real time!

The last update of portfolio was posted on May 4, 2026 and can be found here:

In case someone is interested in the original portfolio reveal post, it’s available here:

2.1. My Private Portfolio

This portfolio tracks my (the main author) real investment journey in individual stocks dating back since 2010.

For privacy reasons, the nominal dollar values are normalised to a $100,000 base. While the actual account balance is pro-forma hidden, all percentage returns, allocation weights are 100% real and accurate.

Thanks for reading Hated Moats! Subscribe for free to receive new posts and support our work.

2.1.1. Main Changes & Weights

Weights

My Top Holdings by weight:

1.) Alphabet remains the usual leader in my portfolio with 29.35% allocation (combined and ).

2.) Nebius has grown to be my second largest holding. This was never really intended but the company has had such an enormous run YTD and at some points, it was up to 12% weight! Too much for me to stomach those crazy moves but I still have short-term conviction in the company. I’m actively selling call options for my entire position with expiry date in Jan 2027, with strike price of $400 per share. This means I’m willing to sell my entire position tax free for gain of +340% and I’m collecting really juicy premiums in the meantime.

3.) Novo Nordisk has recovered somewhat, trying to make $50s its new home, thus growing to be my 3rd largest position.

4.) and 5.) are Cameco , which has had a significant drawdown and , which has been doing quite well, generally.

Overall, my portfolio consists of 22 positions right now and since there has been some major changes in this quarter and I have been unusually active, mainly in June, let’s have a look!

Thanks for reading Hated Moats! This post is public so feel free to share it.

New Buys & Additions to Existing Positions

Remember that you can see my Latest Transactions in the section of the same name on our website:

www.hatedmoats.com

1.) ServiceNow ( ) - ADDED

I bought ServiceNow at 3 occasions since our last update: Once in May (position increased by 50% at $89.03 per share, and 2 times in June at $105.00 (+33.3% increase) and at $90.00 per share (increase of +20% of the position). In this way, I scaled in the position exactly the way I intended, at prices I was happy with, making NOW up to 5% of my position.

The overall average price: $94.25 per share

2.) Compass Pathways ( ) - ADDED

I wanted a slightly bigger exposure in this bet, so I increased the position by +100% at $10.66 per share back in May.

3.) SK Hynix ( ) - NEW

Despite the ugly re-rate recently, I still have faith in the short-term thesis (i.e., under 1 year) and I believe SK Hynix will see it’s new all time high. I could be terribly wrong, and that’s fine since my weight reflects that risk by the under 3% weight of portfolio.

Traded as HY9H.SG, my overall average price: €1253.13 per share

You can ready my thoughts on SK Hynix here:

5.) Neflix ( ) - ADDED

I did an extensive research on the company in the past 6 months, including thorough valuation available here:

and an actually deep “deep dive” analysis available here:

Current weight in portfolio is rather standard 2% and my current average price is $73.98 per share.

Reduced Positions

1.) Adobe ( ) - REDUCED

I reduced my position in Adobe by -30.4% in late June. There were several reasons for this, which I posted in Notes back then - succession risk came into play, there was uncertainty of opportunity cost and my rather large exposure by weight in portfolio. I sold for a loss, and trimmed the position to the weight where I’m happy to wait for this story to play out, now with proper allocation and opportunity cost included in the risk management. The conviction in underlying thesis hasn’t really gotten weaker, but the conviction in timeline of the thesis playing out has. And it showed in my adjustment in position sizing. Was it worth the realised loss and reallocation of the capital? Only time will tell.

Exited Positions

I closed the following positions. The reasoning behind them was “clean-up” of the portfolio. They are all wonderful businesses I wish I owned at much higher portfolio allocation. But since all of them were smaller than 1.5% in portfolio weight, I decided to sell these positions and re-allocate the capital to the stocks where I believe the potential return is higher (ServiceNow, Netflix and Meta):

1.) Waste Management ( ) - CLOSED

Time held: more than 7 years and 2 months

Gain: +101.69%

S&P 500 performance in the same period: +161.71%

Did the stock pick outperformed? : No ❌

Reason to sell: Great defensive stock but it was underperforming long-term, with really small weight and the nominal value of capital makes much more sense being allocated elsewhere, in a more concentrated position.

2.) Visa ( ) - CLOSED

Time held: more than 7 years and 3 months

Gain: +119.46%

S&P 500 performance in the same period: +165.73%

Did the stock pick outperformed? : No ❌

Reason to sell: Exactly same reason as with Waste Management

3.) Interactive Brokers ( ) - CLOSED

Time held: more than 2 years and 9 motnhs

Gain: +308.32%

S&P 500 performance in the same period: +63.97%

Did the stock pick outperformed? : Yes ✔️

Reason to sell: My clean winner, an amazing comany and one of my biggest regrets in terms of not allocating much bigger weight originally. Currently, the weight was very small and again, after the great run, I believe the capital can move the needle more elsewhere. During the next market crash, I will load in this name heavily!

4.) Robinhood ( ) - CLOSED

Time held: more than 4 years and 7 months

Gain: +225.26%

S&P 500 performance in the same period: +60.17%

Did the stock pick outperformed? : Yes ✔️

Reason to sell: Very similar to IBKR. Great business, it had epic run and personally I have an epic story with it - truly a Hated Moat during the GME saga, then dead money for a long time while being deep in red, ended with a redemption arc of massive gains in short period of time. HOOD had it’s massive run and I’m glad I was part of it. It was time to buy ServiceNow instead! :)

2.1.2. Performance

YTD

YTD, it’s been quite a volatile ride, highlighted with Nebius growing to my TOP 2 in holdings and its inherent volatility. As of July 30 close, my YTD performance was on par with the main indices I use as benchamarks (mildly better than S&P 500 and mildly worse than Nasdaq-100):

My Private Portfolio: +10.38%

S&P 500:+9.34%

Nasdaq-100: +11.53%

The main objective and goal - to outperform the market - has not been met yet YTD.

Since Hated Moats Inception (1-year)

However, if we look at 1 year performance (since the start of Hated Moats), the picture gets more clear of having the edge over the broad indices, where I outperform by a large-enough margin. And that matters to me, since I’m a long-term investor:

My Private Portfolio: +32.60%

S&P 500:+18.64%

Nasdaq-100: +21.56%

2.2. Hated Moats Portfolio

“This portfolio started with the first purchase at the time of the first analysis published here, with a clean $100,000 deposit on July 28, 2025. It aims to serve as a transparent portfolio of our analyses here on Substack where every trade and its impact on a $100k base is tracked in real-time. You have enough conviction to say some company is a buy? Put your money where your mouth is! So we did.”

New Buys & Sold / Exited Positions

Literally none. There was no changes in Hated Moats Portfolio in this quarter. No sells, trims, and there was no other way to add since all the capital has been deployed. We’ll consider trimming some positions if attractive-enough Hated Moat opportunities appears. Stay tuned for deep dives & new positions!

Performance

The performance has been interesting. We believe the performance of a portfolio consisting exclusively of Hated Moats should be judged and compared against a benchmark not sooner than 3 years since its inception. We think this is the minimum time that needs to pass to confidently judge where individual theses played out according to our expectations, or not. Still, we’ll have a peak at the YTD and 1-year, i.e. since inception of Hated Moats - performance, just out of curiosity and for accountability:

YTD

Funnily enough, Hated Moats Portfolio, despite being fool of companies with horrible sentiment, was actually outperforming S&P 500 YTD. Slightly underperforming Nasdaq-100 but both are in the area of standard deviation, so we’d call them roughly equally performing. Still quite impressive, to be honest, when you look at the mix of our holdings there. :)

Hated Moats Portfolio: +11.05%

S&P 500:+9.34%

Nasdaq-100: +11.53%

Since Hated Moats Inception (1-year)

On the “Since Inception” (1-year) basis, our Hated Moats Portfolio is underperforming both indices. However, there is one specific reason why and it’s not necessarily bad picks from our side…

And the reason is cash drag. Our measurement of performance is designed to count in cash drag. Our benchamarks’ performances show the return of S&P 500 and Nasdaq-100 as if the whole starting capital, $100,000, was invested in them on day one. There’s no cash drag there and the “real” return is shown. However, we did not deploy the entire capital in the first month. As a matter of fact, our last purchase was by the end of April 2026, meaning that for 3/4 of the entire time (9 months), we still kept cash that “dragged” our performance when compared to “fully invested” performances of indices.

Still, our Hated Moats Portfolio underperformed S&P 500 only by less than 3%. Now that’s a result we take, and we’ll try our best to truly outperform in the second year of the fund.

Hated Moats Portfolio: +15.77%

S&P 500:+18.64%

Nasdaq-100: +21.56%

3. Conclusion

Thank you all so much for being here with us during the first year of Hated Moats.

We’ve had so much fun, which is the most important part, and we’re glad our work brings enough value that you trust us with your e-mail addresses, and deliberately want to read what we have to say.

That truly means a lot.

We’ve managed to publish 80 articles in 52 weeks, spent countless hours researching, writing, polishing the texts, creating infographics and discussing with you - like-minded curious minds.

In the Private Portfolio of main author, I was able to comfortably outperform the market since the inception of Hated Moats, although it’s been a little bit of struggle YTD. On the other hand, our Hated Moats Portfolio is outperforming S&P 500 YTD at the time of publishing this article, and the ouperformance in 1-year (since inception) timeframe is partly caused by cash drag described above. So, performance-wise, we’re reasonably happy.

We also successfully launched our website. All the data seen in this article as far as portfolios are concerned, can be viewed there in real time, anytime, for all of our subscribers:

www.hatedmoats.com

We shared our portfolios, created Valuation Map where you can already browse our valuations of companies from the series of DCFridays and see which comapanies are the most udervalued according to our analysis.

Thanks for being here, truly!
